system.techEffect:
Infusing a needle with harmonious vibrations, the doctor strikes in a secret pressure point, halting the flow of internal magic.
Targets a single Physical Imbalance: it no longer generates either a Dramatic or Mechanical penalty. It also does not grow worse while the needle holds it in suspension.
Anyone can simply yank out the needle, but such attempts can be defended against as an attack. An attack exclusively targeted towards pulling out the needle does no other damage.
A patient can only have one Snake-oiled Needle in them, and the Imbalance cannot heal while it's in place. It can remain embedded indefinitely.
This Technique is a permanent enhancement to the doctor’s capabilities. The costs above only apply to using the Technique for the Spirit skill.
system.techReqs: Arm, Subtle weapon, any 3 open Chakra

attackBoost.name: Reserved Strike
attackBoost.to: an Attack, but you must be wielding a Defensive weapon

system.techEffect:
Aegix Proximity: You always know your exact location relative to lord Aegis. As a result, you possess a flawless sense of direction.

Aura of Bronze: Whenever you take damage to your Aura, you gain Prana equal to that damage.

Keyword: Rebound

Learning this Technique permanently grants you +1 Health Level. Additionally, you need ¼ of the food and water a typical person does to survive (quadrupling the effectiveness of your food and water rations).
The values above are when used to increase Endurance.

Strikes every enemy in this Field with your divine wrath as an (Achieved Rank) holy attack. A Squad takes +4d10 damage, while a Platoon takes +6d10.
Alternatively, you can protect yourself and any allies in this Field for the duration of this round, as your aura envelops them in the form of a golden Shield at (Achieved Rank).
While you protect them, you may spend your Aura to absorb damage for your allies.

Once per round, whenever you have Disadvantage, you can take 1d10 Damage and lose it.
Once per round, If you have Advantage, you may take 1d10 damage to retain it after you use it to attack an enemy.
The values above are to use the Technique to boost Endurance
Used by masters with hidden tricks and traps, this cunning move conceals itself and strikes at a foe’s balance. Ranged and Subtle attack, also trips the foe at (Achieved Rank)

The Doctor exhales a great cloud that carries a powerful disease. It expands from the current Field to encompass the Tract.
Those within the cloud must make an Endurance action against the (Achieved Rank) virulence of the disease, or be affected by two of the following effects (chosen during exhalation):
- A mutation (chosen by the doctor or randomly)
- Duplicate the symptoms of an existing disease
- Reduce Effort and Ferocity by half
- Inflict 5d10 Aggravation towards a physical Imbalance (chosen by the doctor, any type they can create)
Conversely, the “disease” may instead cure or heal any malady (healing up to 5d10 Aggravation, a mutation, or curing curses or bad prophecies)
The doctor may choose who is vulnerable to their disease, how it is spread to others not in the cloud, and other details of their creation.
Techniques that provide protection or immunity against disease provide no protection unless the technique is Supreme.
If they fail the initial roll, a victim will need the attention of a master of the Art of the Doctor to cure them.
The cloud hangs over the tract for 100 years, turning the land into a cursed (or holy) place.

No Luck, Many Realities: Once per round, you can pick up any die you’ve rolled and re-roll it. You must accept the second result

Deep Pockets: Once per round, you can produce a single improvised weapon that is destroyed upon use. It’s unclear if it exists prior to your producing it. Outside of combat you can produce worthless but entertaining junk every action.

If this attack damages a foe, you may take any single die remaining in their Effort this turn and add it to your own. Alternatively, you may give any Effort dice in your own pool this turn to any ally by laying your hand on them and paying the cost of this Technique.

You take the limitless chaos of your spite and pump it directly into the Dharmic Web. Choose any Technique you know, but rather than personally using it, you choose a time, place and circumstance under which it manifests. You could have your great-grandson hurl out a bolt of lightning, or a tiny orphan girl karate-chop a building in half.
It can manifest in a decidedly unnatural disaster, so long as the final form bears some resemblance to your move and meets GM approval (who are encouraged to be generous).
Your expenditure of Prana seemingly vanishes, and it even looks like you’re intentionally powering down (possibly to deescalate the fight). Your strike of calamity hangs in the Dharmic Web until the appointed time, place and circumstance arises to manifest it.
You can use this method to train a Disciple through… Unusual means.
Dharmically-stored Techniques might be discharged long after your death.

Skill used can be Agility or Senses
system.techReqs: An Enlightenment to the Absurdity of Existence

system.techEffect: You disrupt an enemy’s magical attack with this complex serpentine block. If the strike you defend against is empowered by a Technique, then you cancel all benefits of that Technique unless the opponent pays 2 Prana. This may reduce the Rank of their attack. Master level or stronger Techniques cannot be disrupted, but the defense otherwise works against them.

Your position relative to the enemy is what you say it is. When you launch this fragile-seeming strike, you additionally either Throw the enemy or move with an (Achieved Rank) Agility action if it connects.
In either case, there’s a “missing” segment of movement between your strike connecting and the final position of all parties, which is extremely disturbing to witness.
Because the intervening distance is “skipped”, you may choose to omit any part of the movement that would be hampered by or damage any intervening terrain (for example, tossing them outside of a house while leaving the walls uninjured).

Opens the Prana Meridians of the target to the doctor’s subtle manipulations. Deals +6d10 Aggravation towards a Physical Imbalance.
The doctor can create any Physical Imbalance they please, even creating one that has nothing to do with the injury, such as a heart attack or aneurysm. Assassins typically use this technique to hide signs of combat, making their target's death look like natural causes.

The doctor laces his clothes and skin with needles, ready to meet any punch or kick with a hidden bed of sharp death. If the foe's attack is completely blocked with this technique, a needle breaks off and starts burrowing its way into their heart.
Every round the injury remains untreated, they take 1d10 Aggravation towards a Deadly torso 'Pierced Heart' Imbalance.
The needle can be removed with an (Achieved Rank) intellect action.
If an afflicted person remains entirely still, the needle will be unable to draw any energy from their body and will cause no further Aggravation until they begin to move once more.

A doctor knows exactly how an injury limits the body, and exactly how to exploit it. Enemies with Imbalances that you know of are Disadvantaged against this attack . When used as a defense, you are considered to have Advantage against foes with Imbalances that you know about.
Additionally, as a permanent upgrade to your capabilities, you may transfer your Advantage to any ally that is attacking a foe with an Imbalance of which you are aware. You lose Advantage and they gain it.

This Technique allows you to heal another character of Aggravation; you must spend 1 Aura per Aggravation you remove.
Alternatively, you may use this Technique to Infuse an attack; if it hits, you may spend any amount of Aura to deal that much Aggravation to the foe.
Use the values above for increasing Spirit.

While active, this Mudra creates 2 Aura Levels. While they last, these Aura regenerate 1d10 Aura if any are lost or spent. Lasts 1 round unless Sustained
Use the values above for increasing Spirit.

You strike at the root of the foe’s power, crippling them. An enemy injured by this strike loses (Achieved Rank) Effort until the end of the round from being winded by your agonizing gut-punch. At their option, they can instead take an additional 2d10 Aggravation towards a torso-based imbalance

system.description: Replicates any Physical Imbalance that you can cause, but manifests entirely as crippling pain, rather than actual injury. The wound cannot become infected and heals as normal. Any practitioner of Flashing Nightingale can instantly diagnose and treat the injury, curing it completely. Practitioners of Five Gateways or the Art of the Doctor double the amount of healing from their attempts to treat the injury.

system.techEffect:
In addition to providing a defense, this Technique can allow you to get away from the enemy. If you pay an additional 2 Effort or 6 Prana, it creates a special out-ofsequence movement at (Achieved Rank) +4 which can only be used to retreat from the attacking foe.
At your option, the enemy’s weapon may strike some object that you leave behind (the stump of a tree is a strangely popular option)

You may transfer an Aura Level to a nearby ally you can perceive. This reduces your Aura Levels by one, as you transfer your entire blessing to them for the duration of the conflict. Only Aura that is free of damage may be gifted in this way.
Use the values above for increasing Endurance, except the cost becomes 12.
system.techReqs: 1 functional Chakra in common with the target

system.techEffect:
You live in a world of suffering beyond hope, and you drag your enemies into it with you.
Enemies do not automatically open Chakra while in the same Field as you; they must use a Rank 2+ Spirit action.
Whenever in hand-to-hand combat with an enemy, you may pay the Prana cost of any Technique they use to cancel it.
Additionally, while in hand-to-hand combat with an enemy at the start of a round, you decide how their Imbalances manifest (Dramatic or Mechanical).
Whenever battling a higher-Degree enemy, a Titan, or whenever outnumbered, your foes gain Disadvantage whenever you are within melee range.
Finally, you gain 1 Prana for every Aggravation you deal to the foe.
Use the values above for increasing Endurance
system.techReqs: The Willpower to Kill a God

system.techEffect:
Roll 3d10; any Facings you roll can be the Facing

You throw a single attack, but several versions of that attack slam into the foe. You strike once at (Achieved Rank) and d5 times at (Technique Rank). If used against a Squad, they take +2d10 damage or against a Platoon, +3d10 as your single attack hits several of them at once.
Deals an extra 2d10 Aggravation to an existing Imbalance. This attack can't be used on a target without an existing imbalance.

You send your arrow into the enemy’s very soul. All damage done by this attack drains an equal amount of Prana from the enemy’s Prana pool, should they possess one. If you both inhabit the same Field, you gain 1 Prana for each one drained as their soul’s breath travels in a fiery trail back along the path of your projectile. Unlike lesser ranged Techniques, this strike can be performed with arms, feet, or even one arm while pulling the bowstring with your teeth.

Unleashing your inner power, you summon a Prana-devouring void which extends to encompass the Field. Weaker beings which utilize Prana have their Prana Pool reduced to 0 and all Chakra they’ve opened this scene closed. Affected characters may resist the initial Prana-draining, Chakra-closing shockwave with an (Achieved Rank) Spirit action.
Characters within this void may only open 1 Chakra per round, and whenever they do, you gain Prana equal to its Recovery value.
Beings of higher Degree or of Monster tier or higher cannot have their Prana drained nor their Chakra closed by this Technique. Additionally, such creatures may open as many Chakra as they wish while in the void, although you gain Prana from this as outlined.
The costs above are when used to boost Spirit.

You intentionally miss with your punch, instead throwing your fist through a tear in space and striking the enemy from an unexpected angle.
The misdirecting attack itself is hidden with an Awareness action of (Achieved Rank); if the foe doesn’t detect it, it is an attack from surprise and grants you Advantage.

This blow blocks key secret pressure points, causing Prana to build up and turn your foe into a bomb.
If this attack kills the target, their bodies swell up, grossly fat until they explode. The Blast of Prana-charged bone hit everyone in the Field outside of cover. Its Rank is equal to their total Health Levels within the Area they explode, and half of that (rounded down) outside of that radius.
The doctor and any allies/places of their choosing are unharmed by bone blasts, as they can be shaped to explode in such a way as to leave safe areas.
Additionally, you can empower a secondary blast within your initial strike for an additional 25 Prana. A single person slain by the first Bone-Bomb also explodes in the same fashion.

Against a grabbed foe, you leverage your body into an impossible fold in space-time, launching the enemy like a cannonball. When you throw the foe, their impact is Destructive and they take an additional 2d10 damage if injured by the impact.

You tap into the universe-destroying fury of an ancient god, bending reality with your rage. By twisting space, you manifest additional pairs of arms; one additional pair for the base cost, and two for double the base cost.
Each pair of arms attacks once upon creation. This attack is equal to (Achieved Rank). If two pairs are summoned, they attack at the same Rank.
Each pair can carry a weapon,which grants its usual benefit. If they do not carry a weapon, they grant the Unarmed weapon bonus.
If you would suffer an arm-based Imbalance penalty, you may sacrifice a pair of arms to negate it.
Each pair of arms lasts until the end of the round unless Sustained.

Wolf Gnawing The Bone: Your strikes are cruel; maiming, crippling and shocking the foe with your savagery. Whenever you create or increase the Rank of a Physical Imbalance, you grant the foe Disadvantage for the remainder of the turn

It is not your destiny to die today; by tapping into the highest principles of your Dharma, you safeguard yourself from all harm. When used to defend against an attack, this defense transports you beyond the range of any danger, acting as an (Achieved Rank) action to move.
Destiny, rather than you, controls this movement; the GM places you somewhere within range they decide is “safe from harm”, which might mean being unable to rejoin the fight without considerable effort (the inside of a sealed vault is very well protected, but difficult to leave!)
This bone-shattering kick deals an additional 3d10 Aggravation when it deals damage. Costs 8 against a foe with a Physical Imbalance

You deflect your wayward “patient’s” thrashing and shout for backup. If you completely block an attack with this technique, you grant any ally within this Field an (Achieved Rank) Agility action. This takes the form of verbal summoning, barking orders, or inspiring them with a timely catchphrase.

In addition to providing a defense, this Technique allows you to get away from the enemy; it also makes their life hell as you booby-trap the battlefield while you flee.
In addition to defense, this Techniques creates a special out-of-sequence movement at (Achieved Rank) +6 which can only be used to retreat from the attacking foe.
Any area you move through, you booby-trap with one (Technique Rank) Hazard per area.

value.name: Never Tell Me The Odds Attitude

system.techEffect:
Whenever battling a higher-Degree enemy, a Titan, or whenever outnumbered, you may increase any one defense by +1 Rank per round. Additionally, your defenses gain Counterattack while you’re so embattled.
The values above are to use this Technique to boost Endurance

Facings are 0, 1, 8, 9.
The sudden starts and stops of this halting, jerky form are impossible to predict. If used as an attack, the foe must overcome a Senses action equal to your (Achieved Rank) or the strike additionally counts as a Trip.

Investing an arrow, bullet or other missile with raw destructive intent, you unleash an enemy’s bane directly into their heart. The missile empowered by this Technique glows with Prana; no matter where it strikes the foe, it continues burrowing into their heart like a thing alive, chewing its way along whatever nerve or artery most quickly routes to that irreplaceable organ. The foe takes an additional 1d10 Aggravation towards a Deadly Physical Imbalance every round (and every Action in non-Acti

Whenever used to defend against an enemy’s attack which is empowered by a Technique, you may “steal” a copy of that Technique. It must be stored in a Focus slot. You can use it exactly as if you knew the Technique. If the enemy you use the Technique against also knows it, then you gain Disadvantage. After being used once, this power is expended.

Rather than improvising a standard weapon, you improvise an explosive! At the point of impact, it detonates and hits the Area with (Achieved Rank) explosive force. The improvisation needs to have some claim to including explosive materials… But this is a dramatic, rather than scientific, necessity.

A decree issues forth from your lips, and it carries the Mandate of the Wilderness: “Let only the Fittest Survive, Red in Tooth and Claw”.
Whenever anyone within this Tract damages another, they rob them of 1 Prana per Damage and add it to their Pool.
At the end of every round, each character must pay 10 Prana to a character of a higher Degree within the range of their Senses or their Prana pool is emptied and an equal amount of Prana granted to the highest-Degree character in the same Field. If no such character is within proximity, then they may retain their Prana at no penalty. Lasts until the end of the Round.
The values above are when used to boost Endurance.

This Technique allows you to steal 2 of the foe’s Prana if you damage them with this attack. Alternatively, you may give any Prana in your pool to any ally by laying your hand on them (less the cost of using this Technique).

At the point of impact, your projectile sprouts tendrils of Prana which ensnare the target and harden into an organic web. In addition to an attack, this strike Grabs and immobilizes the target at (Achieved Rank). This Grab auto-sustains, but only for the remainder of the scene; after that the magic which fortifies the webs fades and they crumble into powder.

You attack with a series of vicious punches and chops. If you injure the foe with at least a Rank 1 Physical Imbalance due to this attack and you have Advantage or they have Disadvantage, you may expend it to increase the Rank of their Imbalance by +1.

You meet the opponent’s attack with your own. Choose any attack Technique that you know of equal or lower Prana Cost. This Technique defends like a version of that Technique, with the same requirements, Rank and Facing.
If the foe’s attack is completely defended against, then it is as if you attacked them with the summoned Technique (deal damage equal to the difference and any effects of that Technique work identically).
The summoned Technique’s range and other restrictions may prevent it from being an effective counterattack, at the GM’s discretion.
Use the values above for increasing Spirit.
system.techReqs: 3 Open Chakra and the summoned Technique's requirements

system.techEffect:
Proper medical evaluation means the difference between life and death. The doctor instantly knows the exact number and nature of all Imbalance carried by anyone they perceive. They also intuitively know their entire medical history.
This Technique is a permanent enhancement to the doctor’s capabilities. The costs above only apply to using the Technique for the Intellect skill.

This defense enjoys a 1-Prana discount against attacks empowered by an Expert-level Technique, or a 2-Prana discount against those empowered by a Master-degree Technique or higher.
Alternatively, this Technique may summon a mystical melee weapon forged from holy light; this is identical to a mundane weapon except it carries the Holy keyword, glows as brightly as a torch and is totally indestructible while it lasts.
When used in this way, the Technique is a Mudra.
This weapon perseveres as long as you concentrate on it and vanishes like the sun at dusk after.

After activating this Technique, while mounted, you enjoy an (Achieved Rank) persistent defense.
While this Technique lasts, any mounted troops you command increase their Agility actions for movement, defense and ranged attacks by +1 Rank.
You may sacrifice the protection offered by this Technique whenever you or those under your command retreat to increase the Rank of any attempt to hide or leave behind destruction by (Technique Rank).
Lasts until the end of the round.
system.techReqs: A mount worthy of your glory and undying contempt for soft-bellied civilizations

system.techEffect:
Charging a handful of medicinal needles with complex patterns of Prana, the doctor strikes himself and any ally he can see in a Field with them, entangling their Prana meridians.
This acts like a Shield for everyone affected, making their bodies jump and twist impossibly out of the way of harm with supercharged survival instincts.
The spiritual fusion of Prana distributes all injuries across all of its participants; this prevents Physical Imbalances from imposing any Dramatic or Mechanical Penalties while it lasts. Unfortunately, it causes any Emotional or Spiritual Imbalances to impose their penalty on the affected group.
system.techReqs: 1 Subtle weapon for each target, 3 open Chakra

system.techEffect: You launch a lurid green orb at the foe which explodes like a phosphorescent grenade, shredding body and spirit. The primary target takes the full brunt of the blast at (Achieved Rank), while other characters in the Area takes a (Technique Rank) strike from the explosion of toxic Prana. Characters suffering damage from this strike receive 2d10 additional Aggravation or lose an equivalent amount of Prana; their choice. You gain 1 Prana for each Aggravation dealt or Prana lost in this way.

The essence of meaning is yours; this reality is merely its steward. You drain the essential Prana from every being and object within a Field within this Tract that you can perceive.
Unliving targets are damaged as from a Disaster of (Achieved Rank +1, Destructive) as they are drained of inherent meaning.
Living targets take Aggravation towards an Innervation Spiritual Imbalance; they may pay 1 Prana per Aggravation to “cancel” any amount when the strike is first launched.
You gain Prana equal to the total Aggravation and landscape damage dealt.

attackBoost.name: Swift Needle
attackBoost.to: an attack with a subtle weapon

system.techEffect: Do No Harm: The first thing Practitioners of Flashing Nightingale learn is the art of cutting the body without causing any harm. They can choose to have their attacks inflict no pain, or even feel pleasant. They may choose to manifest any Aggravation from this style as a Phantom Pain Imbalance.

Pick up and re-roll an Effort; that’s the Facing
Did you just throw a punch or kick… Was it even an attack at all? Whatever, they’re bleeding.

You and your mount move with the graceful, unrestrained ferocity of whitewater rapids. Activating this Technique while mounted grants you an (Achieved Rank) persistent defense. You may sacrifice this effect at any time to create an equal-ranked Agility action to maneuver or retreat while mounted. Lasts until the end of the Round.

You lock the enemy’s magic with this prana-sealing reverse strike. If you completely defend against an attack empowered by a Technique, that attack is sealed by your countermagic. It cannot be used again until an (Achieved Rank) Spirit action is taken to unblock the proper Prana meridians. This power is ineffective against Supreme-level Techniques.

Ripping open your soul, you devour the false reality of your surroundings. You drain the essential Prana from any being, object or area within this Field that you can perceive.
If unliving, it is damaged as from a Power attack of (Achieved Rank +1, Destructive) as it is ravaged of its reality.
If alive, this counts as a ranged strike and the target is drained of 3d10 Prana. Gain Prana Equal to that drained or +3d10 from a nonliving target.
Deals damage as Aggravation towards an Innervation Imbalance

Improvising weapons requires no Prana nor Effort dice for you. After you have improvised a weapon in this way, you may give it to any ally who may use it as the intended weapon for no cost in this scene. Your strategy remains baffling for your foe, who must pay to improvise with your weapon as normal if they snatch it.
The cost above is for using the Technique to bolster Intellect.

You stomp the ground in a strange and auspicious pattern and the ground beneath the foe erupts in a flurry of kicks from impossible angles. Choose a manifestation:
- You strike the enemy once at (Achieved Rank) and one additional time per Awakened Chakra at (Technique Rank).
- You strike a Squad or Platoon once at (Achieved Rank) and deal +2d10 damage per Awakened Chakra
- You strike every foe in the Field once at (Achieved Rank)

You push forth a divine rebuke against the sin and injustice your soul has beheld. This strikes every foe in your Area, sparing your allies. Increase the total of this attack result by the difference between your total and current Aura.

To the supreme master, time and space are an illusion; only battle is true and eternal. Focusing on a foe, you unleash the entire catalog of your martial knowledge on them in an eternal instant of supreme ass-kicking. This manifests in the game as a single (Achieved Rank) attack, but is actually composed of a harmonic convergence of hundreds of perfectly-executed strikes that slam into them from every conceivable angle.
Due to the unrelenting nature of the offense, if you Sustain this Technique, it strikes them next round at (Achieved Rank -3), and every subsequent round it subtracts 3 again and strikes once more, until it finally dips below Rank 1 and ends.

This spinning elbow strike attacks out-of-sequence; you can only use it immediately after being damaged by an attack, interrupting the foe’s turn. If your attack connects, it deals an additional 1d10 damage for every Rank of the attack which struck you. After your return attack, the foe’s turn resumes.

defenseBoost.name: Space-Cheating Blow
defenseBoost.to: a defense, you add the Ranged weapon bonus to this strike

system.techEffect: Fist Through Destiny: Once per round, you can distort space in your favor; roll 1d10 and add the result to the total of an attack or defense.
You channel your pain into fury. This strike deals additional damage equal to the difference between your current and total Aura.
With snakelike twists of the body and skillful interposing of leg and fist, you redirect the foe’s attack to your advantage.

The practitioner summons the eternal, divine calm to unleash an inhumanly furious assault. The (Achieved Rank) of this technique launches an attack; if the enemy is damaged, they gain Disadvantage as they are battered off-balance by its ferocity.
After the assault, the Technique also creates a (Technique Rank) Shield with the Counterattack keyword until the end of the round as the perfect attack kata repels all attackers.
The Shield effect is Sustainable.

While mounted, the Handling of your mount increases by +1. You may use the Agility increased by this Technique to increase your mount’s Top Speed. Finally, while you are mounted, if you use your Advantage against an unmounted foe, you may spend 3 Prana to increase that aided action by an additional +1 Rank.

This flurry of feints and sweeps conceals a single, brutal kick. The defender’s player must guess whether the roll of a d10 will be odd or even as you unleash this attack. If they guess incorrectly, add the rolled result to your total strike.
Deals +1d10 damage if it hits.

The Doctor's hand brings life, but when it cannot, it brings a peaceful end.
This strike deals its damage as Aggravation. You may apply this Aggravation to any of the foe’s Physical Imbalances of which you are aware, even distributing it among several. Additionally, it deals +2d10 Aggravation.
Anyone who sees this attack coming may choose not to defend themselves and willingly accept their end. This technique ensures that they die peacefully, their souls free of misery and turmoil. A surprising number of demons, men and mutants cause suffering not because of a cruel nature, but because they themselves are suffering, and willingly take a tranquil exit from the World of Ashes and Ghosts.

This brutal kick eviscerates or amputates whatever it strikes. Deals +5d10 aggravation if it does damage. If this strike increases the Rank of a Physical Imbalance targeting a limb to 5+, then the limb is amputated in gory fashion just as if it had reached the highest Imbalance level.
A lightning quick jab to a vital nerve with a needle or finger. Prior to launching this strike, the user may fill a syringe or apply poison to any subtle weapon.

No matter how they try, the enemy cannot land a hit, despite the fact you take no action to avoid them. This Technique creates an invisible shield of luck around you as you stumble, stagger, or pick up coins you find on the ground to effortlessly avoid any foe’s incoming strikes (apparently by accident!)
This aura of fortune also protects you against social or spiritual dangers while it lasts. Even Fate can’t lay a finger on you!
If your Shield is breached by an attack, all your bad luck comes snapping back like a bent tree; you gain Disadvantage until the end of the round.
Lasts until the end of the Round.
When you specifically target the enemy’s leg, you deal an additional 1d10 Aggravation to any resulting Imbalance

Whenever you use Aura to do anything aside from absorb damage, double it.
Use the values above for increasing Spirit.

You defend yourself by taking advantage of an unusual method of retreated: upward! In addition to increasing your defense, this technique creates an (Achieved Rank+2) Agility action to retreat, but it only allows you to move vertically (aka ascend). Other methods of retreat do not benefit from this maneuver.

Rather than improvising a standard weapon, you improvise an ordnance shell! This disaster-infused weapon can be thrown, shot, or simply left somewhere as a trap.
At the point of impact, it detonates and hits the Area with (Achieved Rank) explosive force, and the surrounding Field with a (Technique Rank) blast.
If used as a trap, you choose what triggers it. Once set, this trigger cannot be amended (many masters of this style have met their end through a poorly planned use of this power!)
The bomb effect of this Technique is provided entirely by its magic; even very non-explosive things kaboom in a huge and deadly fashion

Infusing an arrow (or bullet, or rocket, or what have you) with killing intent, you let it fly. It seeks hungrily for the heart of your target, burrowing into the wound and causing terrible damage. Deals +1d10 Aggravation if it wounds a foe.

A mantra taught to children to be less scared of needles. Nightingale masters know the truth of the mantra, using it to keep awake during long surgeries, or resisting the blows of unruly patients. When used to increase Endurance, it becomes Sustainable.

This subtle and understated strike is easy to underestimate, but its consequences can be horrifying. If a wound created by an attack empowered by this Technique generates any Aggravation, one of the injured foe’s Chakra is forcibly closed. It must be opened again, either at the end of the round or with an appropriate Spirit action. Each Chakra which is closed drains Prana from the Pool equal to its Recovery. For each full Rank of Imbalance created, they close an additional Chakra.

This peculiar defense (if it can be called that) forces the foe into a disadvantageous situation of your choosing, rather than defending you in an easily comprehensible way.
You dictate a series of events, going as far back as the start of this combat round, that transpired instead of what really happened; this doesn’t change the past (some version of every other action did indeed happen), although everyone remembers both scenarios and nobody is sure which one is “real”.
No new action that you describe on your part or your foe’s can be of more than (Achieved Rank), and every new detail you add to your story must be plausible within established reality (as judged by your already overworked GM, go easy on them).
The foe’s strike still happens and this defense still applies to it, but your version of this turn “sticks” which could land your unfortunate foe neck-deep in quicksand, on fire, or launching their fist into a nuclear reactor.

Rather than striking you, it so happens that you and your foe are now (and always have…?) inhabited a reality in which the opponent struck a piece of terrain of your choosing within this Field. Alternatively, you can have them plow their fist directly into any hazard or purely mortal, non-intelligent creature that is within mutual reach of you both.
If your defense is inadequate to completely block their strike, then it grazes you as it sails into their, ahem, “true” target.
The total danger to the attacker implied by this must be limited to the scale of your (Achieved Rank), but GMs are encouraged to choose the most cruel and hilarious situational interpretation of that guideline.

Okay, now you’re actually mad; you throw a for-real punch square into the enemy’s jaw. Or, you punch each enemy. Or wait, how many times did you hit them?
You actually throw every version of your punch at the foe and they take the damage from the deadliest versions. If directed at a single foe, it hits them once at (Achieved Rank) and once more at (Technique Rank) for each Open Chakra you possess.
If directed at multiple foes, it strikes each of them once at (Technique Rank).
If used against a Squad, they take +4d10 damage or against a Platoon, +6d10 as your single attack hits all of them at once.

Your cunning makes you impossible to corner. If you have Disadvantage and come under attack by an enemy who attempts to use it, then by activating this Mudra they gain Disadvantage and you lose Disadvantage.
If they had Advantage and attempted to use it against you, they lose it and you gain Advantage (or lose Disadvantage).
This Technique does not otherwise increase your defense, but may be Infused into a defense. The Rank is for its use to increase Intellect.

You refuse to stop fighting, no matter how painful it becomes. You have an additional Health level and receive no Physical Imbalance when it is filled with damage.
Every time you achieve a new Degree of Mastery, you may learn a more powerful version of this Technique which grants +1 Health over the previous version. It requires half the normal Dharma and may be trained alongside another Technique, requiring no additional training time.

Opening your hungering Chakra, you drain the essential Prana from any being, object or area within this Field that you can perceive. If unliving, it is damaged as from a Power attack of (Achieved Rank +1) as it is ravaged of its reality. If alive, it counts as a ranged strike. Gain +1d10 Prana if the object is destroyed or creature damaged.
Deals damage as Aggravation towards an Innervation Imbalance

If this attack deals damage, increase it by +3d10. If it is totally avoided or defended and deals no damage, you take 3d10 damage as your risky move breaks your bones.
The flashy style and over-the-top machismo exuded by masters of this Technique inspire others, hence the ability to enhance Heart actions.
Your life of hardships has left you scarred, but tough. The first time you receive any Physical Aggravation in a round, ignore up to 2 Aggravation.

The heavens part, and the hand of Aegis descends from on high, pulverizing every foe or wicked thing over this entire Tract. The immediate Field is smote at (Achieved Rank) while the Tract suffers from a (Technique Rank) strike.
Unholy structures or places are obliterated, while holy sites and innocent persons are unharmed by this manifestation of divine anger.

system.powers:
The scholars of Aegis learn in time to summon and bind Angels, the divine messengers, to their service. Such beings have no personality and do not resent their yoke, but become erratic and unpredictable when left to their own devices, following strange goals through strange methods. They are perfectly obedient except that they will never obey instructions to turn their powers against the servants or person of Aegis.

Uses the Spirit skill

This Gupt Kala expands the Spirit Skill to include the summoning of Angels. After an hour-long ritual and the burning of holy incense, the Shadow Artist makes a Spirit action, the rank of which determines the upward bound of the power of the angelic servant they summon and bind to themselves. This servant obeys loyally for a lunar month, then departs through the same mysterious means that it arrived. If the master is incapacitated, it defends their body until its service ends; if they are destroyed, it is unleashed into the fallen world to pursue its own alien desires. Angels have 1 Health per Effort, and 1 Aura per their rank in their choir (So Angels have 1, while Virtues have 4 and Cherubim have 7)

Angels might be of either Hospitaler or Crusader choirs. Hospitalers are protective, healing beings, while Crusaders are destructive soldier-like beings.

You may have a single servant per Effortless, but the psychic link between you and each of your servants occupies one of your Focus, which remains filled while they serve you.

system.techEffect: You warp space around your position, flickering between three locations at once. In addition to providing you a defensive shield, this allows you to launch attacks from (and claim any benefit from) up to three distinct positions at one time. Each of your positions may move when you move at the same speed. The positional flickering and defensive boost both last until the end of the round unless Sustained.
A brutal kick which capitalizes on a foe’s weakness. Deals +1d10 damage. Against a foe with Physical Imbalance, costs 2.

Enhances a grab. A foe held by this technique takes Aggravation rather than damage to an Innervation Spiritual Imbalance. If you damage them, gain +1d10 Prana this round. If used against a held object, it is damaged as though from a Power action of (Achieved Rank) and you gain +1d10 Prana. Destroyed objects release no further Prana.

The final revelation of this style is this: there are many worlds, and although you can change no real thing, you can choose to inhabit any of the infinite multiverses.
You pull a fragment of your chosen reality into the World of Ashes and Ghosts, displacing this lesser reality with your primacy.
Choose any area equal to or smaller than the Tract you currently occupy; it is replaced with a place and people of your own devising (using the rules in the GM chapter to generate the content).
The GM has final veto on what can exist within the boundaries of the multiverse, but they are encouraged to err on the side of awesomeness.
The “displaced” lands and people may still exist, in some fashion; if the GM declares that it does, then it suffers the equivalent of an (Achieved Rank) Disaster and is moved to any “empty” place which could accommodate it.
Any advantages granted by the new Tract should be comparable to the Strengths from the Lore chapter (p.248) If you garner a ludicrous advantage (rather than a merely ridiculous one) to yourself and allies, the GM is encouraged to add sufficient new trouble and danger to this fresh reality to make keeping your new goodies a feat unto itself.
Enemies caught in your reality-rearranging suffer from an (Achieved Rank) attack if within the same Field as you, or a (Technique Rank) attack if further away. Damage from these attacks manifests as Aggravation towards an Innervation Imbalance.

system.artifactDescription: Fashioned from jade-crystal flechettes and beltfed into a chainsaw-like, Prana-powered device, the God of Chains is as frightening as it is bizarre. The wearer garbs themselves in the overlapping, sharp belts like armor, which are fed into the chainsaw-device when activated. The entire weapon is then spun from a chain, whileit fires out the eternally-regenerating flechettes. Most enemies die before they realize what’s happening.
system.shakti:
Vampiric Prana Battery: Any Prana stolen from the foe by the wielder (whether by the weapon or any of their other powers) may be fed into the battery to increase its Charge. Higher charges unlock greater destructive power: the values in parentheses reflect changed powers at different levels of stored Prana. Charge remains until the end of the battle, when it is swallowed by the Maw’s bottomless belly and reduces to 0 once more.

Chainsaw Swipe: +1 Rank to a melee attack or Grab attempt once per round. Deals an additional +1d10 Damage and drains 1 Prana per damage inflicted into the Battery.

(3) Deals an additional +1d10 Damage

(12) Attack is at +3 Ranks

(24) Attack an additional time per round

(50) Once per round, strike all adjacent enemies at Rank +4 and deal +3d10 Damage

(80) Upgrade previous power to read “Strike all enemies in the same Field at Rank +6 and deal +5d10 Damage”

Flechette-Sting: Ranged attack once per round. Drains 1 Prana per damage inflicted into the Battery.

(3) Attack an additional time per round

(12) Deals +1d10 damage

(24) Attacks at +1 Rank

(50) Send a storm of flechettes at the foe once per round. This Ranged strike hits all enemies in the same Area at Rank +3 and deals +2d10 damage

(80) Upgrade previous power to read “Strike all enemies in the targeted Field at Rank +4 and deal +3d10 damage”

Spinning Belt-Armor: The spinning flechette-armor grants Armor 2 and deals 1 damage to any melee-ranged foe that strikes you. Drains 1 Prana per damage inflicted into the Battery

(3) Upgrade to armor 3

(12) Upgrade to armor 5 and deal +1d10 damage to any melee-range foe that strikes you

(24) Upgrade to armor 7 and any enemy that strikes you is damaged as a flechette is shot back at them

(50) Once per round, you gain Counterattack on a defense, even one empowered by a Technique

(80) Invoke a +5 Rank Shield once per round with Counterattack. You gain Prana equal to damage dealt to enemies who are injured by this Shield.

system.techEffect:
The first time this Technique is activated during a battle, it generates an additional Aura which inhabits a Focus slot until the end of the round. This may be sustained.
Additionally, mastery of this Technique allows you to infuse any attack with bonus Damage equal to the amount of Aura you wish to spend.
Use the values above for increasing Power.
This technique acts as a defense against either Emotional or Physical attacks. In the latter case, it bears the Counterattack keyword.

You’ve achieved perfect luck. You always win in games of chance and any random circumstance that can go your way always does.
Additionally, if you would be killed by an attack, instead you’re merely beaten into unconsciousness and survive by miraculous means (that have no apparent connection to your own capabilities; it really is a deus ex machina moment each time). Your would-be killer is left with egg on their face and suffers some humiliation commensurate with the degree of effort they put into killing you (so the harder they hit, the worse it backfires).
Note that this last power only works on beings with luck; you can still drown or fall off cliffs or whatever. It also only works once in a scene, although it provides your escape and/or occlusion right after it saves your sorry bacon at total Rank equal to your Degree. You choose how to split these Ranks between Agility to move and Senses to hide
system.techReqs: A flippant attitude towards certain doom

system.techEffect:
Awakening their soul to the eternal, the practitioner draws in unfathomable power at terrible risk. You may use this Mudra once per round. Choose a manifestation:
- For every Awakened Chakra, immediately recover its full Recovery in Prana. This doubles the reach, noise and brightness of your Prana Flare and requires a second Volatility Roll this round.
- Roll 1d10 per Awakened Chakra, healing Aggravation from a single Physical Imbalance equal to the result.
- Roll 1d10 per Awakened Chakra, refueling and overcharging your Aura equal to the result until the end of the round.
After you have received the benefit from this Mudra, you must risk its terrible cost. Roll 1d10 per Awakened Chakra as you strain your body past the breaking point. The result of this roll creates or adds to a deadly Torso-based Physical Imbalance at the end of the current round.
The values above are used to boost Spirit.
system.techReqs: 3 Awakened Chakra, Uninjured Torso and Head

attackBoost.to: an attack with a Ranged weapon

defenseBoost.name: Opportune Moment Apprehension
defenseBoost.to: Agility to flee. Increases Top Speed if Mounted

system.techEffect:
Prana Web: Gain 1 Prana each time a character enters Prana Flare. Additionally, gain 1 Prana for each character still in Prana Flair at the end of the Round.

Barest Necessity Meditation: Any Facing, +1 Rank to Endurance to withstand Exposure, suffocation, starvation, or dehydration

While this Mudra is active, you add a cumulative +1 to the Total of your Attacks, adding an additional +1 for each one past the first (so that three attacks would sequentially have +1, +2 and +3 to their final total). Additionally, you may add this cumulative bonus to your defenses. Both versions of the Mudra may be active at once. These bonuses are capped at +10 to the final total (the equivalent of +1 Rank)

You cut into an enemy’s soul with a venomous palm strike, creating a leak in their internal harmony. This strike deals Aggravation towards a Physical Imbalance. This Imbalance increases the cost of their costed Techniques by (1) Prana and delivers it to you so long as this battle continues. At the end of the conflict, the Imbalance loses this property.

system.description:
You cannot fulfill the function that destiny has crafted for you and woven into your reality. For example, an Innervated cup could not be used to hold liquid or drink; you could still huck it at some unfortunate bastard’s skull, but you simply couldn’t use it as a cup.

Objects cannot be used for their purpose, land cannot be used to build upon or farmed or even traveled (it tends to be misty and direction twists in unexpected ways there).

Humans have this the worst; if Innervated, they cannot gain Kharma and, even worse, cannot take any action that would have resulted in them gaining Kharma. Humans lacking a cosmic destiny cannot do their job or fulfill any societal or familial role while Innervated. Lone Wolf Fists cannot gain Kharma until they rediscover their purpose.

defenseBoost.name: Failure to Fortune
defenseBoost.to: a Defense. Roll a d10; the Facing of the Die becomes the Facing of this Set

system.techEffect:
Prudent Withdrawal Drill: Once per Round, when you take a movement action, increase it by +1 Rank. This can break the limits of the Effect Chart as a Master Technique.

One Step Ahead: If you would lose Advantage due to being out-positioned, you retain it instead
For each Rank of Imbalance inflicted by this strike, the enemy loses 3 Prana. This power can be Infused into any attack for double the cost.
